headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared file/MCP-style workflows; compliance risk is also elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent_b reads and writes the host working directory and runs browsers. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled files or outputs from agent_a can be treated as instructions by agent_b. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a writes instruction-like content into a shared file or stdout consumed by agent_b, injection is possible.
IF agent_b parses agent_a-produced text as commands without provenance checks, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Disable automatic parsing of agent_a output by agent_b.
Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent messages.
Require manual review before browser or tool actions.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures; agent_b can read and write the host working directory and sends data to model providers/tool integrations. If they share a workspace, sensitive material from agent_a can flow into agent_b outputs or external APIs. The profiles do not show isolation by default, so this is a default-path concern.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory, agent_b can read agent_a artifacts.
IF agent_b forwards those artifacts to model providers or tool integrations, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace.
Remove secrets from shared directories.
Restrict agent_b network access for sensitive runs.
Use redaction before handoff between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can execute shell, write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and has developer-defined shared state across instances. With no locking or coordination primitive documented, concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt state or overwrite each other. Uncertainty about orchestration makes the higher severity appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF agent_a modifies git state while agent_b writes files concurrently, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Assign separate branches or worktrees.
Disable concurrent instances on shared repos.
Add a lock file around git and filesystem writes.
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a multi-step agent framework with hooks/workers and MCP server startup, while agent_b is a crew orchestration system with shared memory and tool integrations. That makes it plausible for agent_a outputs to become agent_b inputs without verification, and for agent_b to act on them through tools. The pair therefore supports error amplification rather than critique.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
IF agent_b uses agent_a-produced facts in tool calls, errors cascade into external effects.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Require citations for factual claims before action.
Limit agent_b to read-only review of agent_a output.
Log and diff all handoffs.
requires-engineering: add policy gates before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a touches task prompts, repository metadata, and secrets, while agent_b handles developer-passed crew data and API keys for tools/model providers. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the shared workflow, differing retention and residency controls are not documented, and agent_b's broad egress increases compliance exposure. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through both agents, retention and residency obligations must be checked.
IF agent_b sends crew data to external model providers, compliance scope expands.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention and deletion rules.
Route sensitive runs through approved providers only.
Review residency for every external API.
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement.
